- When sentiment turns bullish (↑ sentiment change) and news volume spikes, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often fails to mean-revert; delay correction by 1–2 periods unless sentiment shifts downward.
- If sentiment remains flat or negative for 3+ consecutive days, model overestimates recovery — lower forecast by 3–5%.
- In low-news periods, model underestimates volatility — increase forecast variance or add 2–3% buffer for downside risk.
- When sentiment is neutral and price is trending upward, model often underestimates momentum — add 1–2% to forecast for continuation.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment shifts.
- In high-news environments, model tends to overfit short-term noise — filter out 1–2% of extreme outliers in forecast sequence.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often fails to adjust downward — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next period.
- Model underestimates downward moves when sentiment is weak and news is low — add 1–3% downward buffer for low-sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is positive but news is low, model overconfident — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
